{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer in 90 days, and A's payers are businesses with existing budgets. Price anchors are sourced: SwagUp's $99/mo floor, Sendoso's estimated $15k-$20k+/yr platform fee, and $30-75 per onboarding kit. A single B2B customer could plausibly pay a meaningful amount.",
    "B's payer is an individual consumer, anchored at $1.99/month. By the brief's own count there are at least four free, maintained competitors, several of them open source, so willingness to pay is undermined directly. Reaching even modest revenue would need install volume that the brief says organically takes 3-6 months.",
    "A has a plausible niche: solo-founder pricing, Stripe-only, priced below SwagUp's minimum. It also has a free channel, the Stripe App Marketplace. B's differentiator is still an open question.",
    "B has product-risk problems a solo operator can't easily absorb: noisy detection with false accusations, dependence on DOM structures it doesn't control, and possible ToS conflicts. A's logistics risk is real, but the brief says it can be offloaded to existing fulfillment APIs with no inventory held.",
    "Neither brief shows strong demand. A's demand evidence is thin, but B's evidence is complaints about bots rather than signals of intent to pay, so B gains no edge on demand."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence consists of Reddit users venting about bots and a CEO acknowledging AI spam. That shows the problem exists, not that anyone will pay to filter it. The only price anchor is ReviewGuard's $1.99/month Pro tier, with no data on how many people pay it. The brief itself notes that no competitor publishes install or revenue numbers.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. Both briefs are weak on demand. A's only new signal is a LinkedIn comment from a gift recipient, and every named A competitor already offers event-triggered swag. A wins mainly because of the B2B payer and the presence of sourced business price points, not because its demand is proven. A's physical logistics and enterprise-style sales could still keep it from closing a customer within 90 days."
}
